title: The Last 24 Hours on Earth
subtitle: Choices, priorities and what really matters

slides.title: The Last 24 Hours on Earth
slides.question: If you knew you had only 24 hours left, what would you do first?
slides.summary: Breaking news: scientists have confirmed that a massive asteroid will hit Earth in exactly 24 hours, and there is no known way to stop it. One day, one planet, no second chances. The question uses the second conditional: If you knew…, what would you do?

expressions.meaning: an imaginary situation now (second conditional).

expressions.en: The first thing I'd do is…
expressions.meaning: a clear way to start your answer.
to say what you prefer.
you can't try again.

items.question: What have scientists confirmed?
items.explain: Present perfect (have confirmed) for recent news.

items.question: Can anyone stop the asteroid?
items.explain: "There is no known way to…" = nobody knows how to…

items.question: If you knew you had only 24 hours left, what would you do first?
blocks: and tell them I love them.
items.explain: If + past (knew, had), then would + verb.

slides.title: The First Decision
slides.question: 24 hours left. What really matters now?
slides.summary: With only 24 hours left, you have to decide what really matters. The slide asks about three things: the people you would spend the day with, something you've been putting off, and what you would leave behind or hold on to.

expressions.meaning: contact someone, often to reconnect or offer support.
delay doing something.
use something as well as possible.
keep something; not let it go.
slowly accept a difficult situation.
leave it when you go; what remains after you.

items.question: If you could spend your final day with only three people, who would you choose and why?
blocks: my wife, my mother and my best friend,

items.question: Is there anything you've been putting off that you would finally do?
blocks: so I would finally reach out to him.
items.explain: put off + noun (have been putting off); reach out TO someone.

items.question: What would you leave behind, and what would you want to hold on to?
blocks: my best memories with my family.
items.explain: leave behind / hold on to + noun.

slides.title: Your Time Is Limited. Your Choices Matter.
slides.question: You can only choose three experiences from the six options.
slides.summary: You have 24 hours left, but you cannot do everything. Choose three of six experiences: A Family, B Adventure (a place you've always dreamed of seeing), C Reconciliation (someone you've lost touch with), D Helping others, E A dream, F Solitude.

expressions.meaning: compare the advantages and disadvantages before deciding.
decide that something is not an option.
stop having or doing something.
decide to do something you planned.
give up something important for something else.
a chance you will probably never have again.

items.question: Which three experiences would you choose, and why?
blocks: because people matter more to me
items.explain: "matter more to me than…" compares what is important.

items.question: Which option would be the hardest to give up?
items.explain: give up + noun; gerund as subject: seeing Paris is…

items.question: Would your choices reveal who you really are, or simply what you value most at this moment?
blocks: what I value most right now,
they also show who I am.
items.explain: weigh up is separable: weigh everything up.

slides.title: Wait… There's a Chance!
slides.question: The world is holding its breath.
slides.summary: Breaking news: scientists have discovered a 5% chance that the asteroid will miss Earth completely. However, nobody can confirm what will happen, and the impact is still expected in 24 hours. The world is holding its breath.

expressions.meaning: say something is impossible: We can't rule out a miracle.
keep hoping.
prepare yourself for something bad.
even though it seemed very unlikely.
a very small chance.
not knowing what will happen.

items.question: Would you change your plans now, or stick to your original decisions?
items.explain: stick TO your decisions = not change them.

items.question: Is it better to prepare for the worst or hold on to hope?
blocks: but still hold on to hope.
items.explain: brace yourself FOR; hold on TO.

items.question: Would people become more selfish or more generous in this situation?

slides.title: The Final Phone Call
slides.question: Some things are too important to leave unsaid.
slides.summary: Imagine you can make one final phone call. Who would you call, what would you finally say, and what if they didn't answer or reacted differently from what you expected? Some things are too important to leave unsaid.

expressions.meaning: finally say something that has been worrying you.
do something to correct a past mistake.
not value someone because they are always there.
be extremely important to someone.
I can't find the words to express this.

expressions.en: say what needs to be said
expressions.meaning: say the important thing, even if it's difficult.

items.question: Who would you call, and why have you waited so long to have this conversation?
blocks: because I have taken him for granted
items.explain: take someone FOR GRANTED (past participle: taken).

items.question: What would you finally tell this person that you've never had the courage to say?
blocks: that he means the world to me
items.explain: mean the world TO someone; get something off your chest.

items.question: What if they didn't answer, or their reaction wasn't what you expected?
items.explain: Second conditional: If he didn't…, I would…

slides.title: The Last Broadcast
slides.question: Your final message to the world. Speak for 2 minutes.
slides.summary: You have two minutes on a live broadcast to send a final message to the world. Talk about a lesson for humanity, one thing you would change if you could start again, and a message that should never be forgotten.

expressions.meaning: finally; after everything.
the most important thing.
leave something good for the people after you.
have a positive effect on someone or something.

items.question: A lesson for humanity: What should people learn from our existence?
items.explain: "What really matters is…" introduces your main idea.

items.question: One thing I'd change: What would you do differently if you could start again?
blocks: I would worry less about work
items.explain: If I could…, I would… + comparatives (less, more).

items.question: A message that matters: What should never be forgotten?
items.explain: make a difference / leave a legacy.

practice.prompt: I've been ___ calling my old friend for months.
practice.explain: put off = delay. After "been" we use -ING: putting off.
practice.tip: "I keep putting off my tax return."

practice.prompt: Let's make the most ___ the time we have.
She finally came to terms ___ the news.
I would reach to my brother and say sorry.
accept: I would reach out to my brother and say sorry.
practice.explain: The phrasal verb is reach OUT TO someone.
practice.tip: "Feel free to reach out to me if you have questions." (common in emails)

practice.prompt: After weighing ___ all the options, I chose family.
Build the sentence: a hard choice.
practice.explain: weigh up = compare; go ahead with = do what you planned.
practice.tip: Useful in meetings: "Let's go ahead with option B."

practice.prompt: There's only a ___ chance that the asteroid will miss Earth.
practice.explain: a slim chance = a very small chance.

practice.prompt: Against all ___, the asteroid missed Earth.
practice.explain: against all odds = although it was very unlikely.

practice.prompt: We can't ___ the possibility that it will miss.
practice.explain: rule out = say something is impossible.

practice.prompt: I took my parents for grant for years.
accept: I took my parents for granted for years.
practice.explain: The expression is take someone for granted.

practice.prompt: She means the world for me.
accept: She means the world to me.

practice.prompt: I need to get this off my ___.
practice.explain: get something off your chest = finally say it.

practice.prompt: I want to make ___ for the mistakes I made.
practice.explain: make amends = correct a past mistake.

practice.prompt: If I ___ (have) only 24 hours, I ___ (call) my family first.
practice.explain: Second conditional: If + past simple, would + verb.

practice.prompt: If you could start again, what ___ you do differently?
Build the sentence: if they didn't answer.
